svg.title: Buffer Pool Replacement Policies: CLOCK, 2Q, and LIRS
svg.desc: Animated three-panel diagram comparing scan-resistant buffer pool replacement policies: CLOCK circular hand sweeping frames and clearing usage_bit from 1 to 0 before evicting an unpinned 0-bit victim; 2Q separating single-pass sequential scans in A1in and A1out ghost queue from recurrent hot pages in Am; and LIRS distinguishing Low Inter-Reference Recency (LIR) pages from High Inter-Reference Recency (HIR) pages.
svg.text: Buffer Pool Replacement Policies: CLOCK, 2Q & LIRS
Lock-free second-chance sweeps and scan-resistant admission isolating hot B-Tree pages from sequential scan pollution
Atomic usage_bit=1 on hit (no global LRU mutex).
Sequential scan pages never pollute hot Am LRU.
New page enters A1in; re-reference via A1out ghost
proves recurrence before granting scarce Am slots.
Ranks by Inter-Reference Recency (IRR), not age.
Handles looping scans > cache size far better
than strict LRU without manual tuning.
Hand clears usage_bit on first pass
LIRS promotes HIR page P5 to LIR
Am & LIR stay hot in RAM
